original_finding.evidence: The proof invokes a parallel pseudoreal/SU(2) real structure for the twisted product Dirac operator. A unitary connection on the underlying Hermitian bundle need not preserve the specified SU(2) reduction, so that real structure need not be parallel and the cited product-kernel parity result does not apply as stated. excerpts: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Assume full Axiom of Choice for the analytic product-kernel and mod-two-index calculation on every index-one background below, as well as for the concrete round-sphere benchmark. The finite-dimensional inverse-determinant sign calculation itself needs no additional choice principle. Let $M=S^4$ have its boundary orientation, a specified smooth Riemannian metric, and the standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean $5$-ball. Here a spin structure means a principal right $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle $Q\to M$ with a smooth equivariant double-cover map to the principal $\mathrm{SO}(4)$-bundle $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(M)$ of positively oriented orthonormal frames, covering $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$. Let $\Delta^\pm$ be the complex half-spin representations with representation maps $\rho_\pm$, and let $S^\pm=Q\times_{\rho_\pm}\Delta^\pm$ be their associated bundles; the Levi-Civita connection lifts to $Q$. Let $E\to M$ be a smooth rank-two Hermitian bundle with structure group $SU(2)$ and smooth unitary connection $A$. Treat $SU(2)$ as a nondynamical background global symmetry and consider the chiral Dirac family for one massless left-handed Weyl doublet in the fundamental representation. Use the Clifford convention $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2g(v,w)$ for $v,w\in T_xM$, and the tensor-product spin and gauge connection in $D_A^+=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(M;S^-\otimes E)$. Here $(e_i)$ is any positively oriented local orthonormal frame and the expression is frame-independent. The $H^1$ norm is $\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|\nabla u\|_2^2$ and $L^2$ uses the bundle metric and Riemannian volume; these are complex Hilbert spaces, and the smooth first-order expression defines a bounded map between them. For complex Banach spaces $X,Y$, a bounded complex-linear map $T:X\to Y$ is Fredholm when its range is closed and both $\ker T$ and $\operatorname{coker}T:=Y/\operatorname{ran}T$ are finite dimensional; its index is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}T:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker T-\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}T$. Put $n_+=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D_A^+$ and $n_-=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$. Assume this bounded chiral realization is Fredholm with $n_+-n_-=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+=1$; this is the index-one-sector hypothesis. The chosen boundary line in this theorem is the inverse determinant line $\mathcal L_A=(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D_A^+)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$, equipped with the supplied Quillen metric and Bismut--Freed unitary connection. This explicitly selects the complex chiral determinant line; no identification with the fermionic Pfaffian line of a pseudoreal path-integral presentation is asserted. For $N$ independent identical doublets use $\mathcal L_A^{\otimes N}$. For a proved concrete instance, assume full AC and take the unit round metric, $E=S^+$ and the positive-spin Levi-Civita connection: its complex chiral kernel has dimension $1$, its cokernel dimension $0$, and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-1$ in the convention $c(E)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$. The conditional conclusion below still applies to every stipulated index-one background; this concrete instance supplies that index by proof rather than as a physical postulate.
